item.title: Players in limbo after NZ netball league collapses
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Players in limbo after NZ netball league collapses

All Parris Mason has known is playing netball. But with a World Cup just nine months away, she and four other New Zealand players have been left in limbo after the collapse of their domestic league.

"There's a high potential I will not be playing netball heading into a World Cup," she told BBC Sport.

While a significant number of her Silver Ferns team-mates play professionally in Australia and England, Mason stayed with her home league.

The 23-year-old defender, who has been a full-time professional for six years, found out her netball fate when the news was leaked to the media.

"It shattered me," she said. "The influx of emotions; is my career over? What do I do next? It was just so much to handle all at once."

Netball New Zealand admitted the way events unfolded publicly was deeply regrettable and has pledged to support the affected players.

"We know this period of uncertainty has been extremely tough for players, coaches, teams and everyone involved in the domestic competition," a statement said.

"Their wellbeing is our priority, and we are working closely with the New Zealand Netball Players' Association to support them."

It comes as the Silver Ferns are on the cusp of becoming the world's number one ranked side, after winning gold at the 2026 Commonwealth Games and beating Australia in the Constellation Cup.

The World Cup will be held in Sydney, Australia, between 25 August and 5 September, with New Zealand looking to win the title for a sixth time.

What happened to the ANZ Premiership?

There had been uncertainty over the future of the ANZ Premiership for a couple years. The league had struggled to secure long-term broadcast deals which impacted the league financially.

In 2026, the league recorded a loss of around $NZ 3.7m (Â£1.5m). There was an exodus of the country's best players.

Ten of the 12 Silver Ferns who won gold for New Zealand at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow have moved overseas to play - primarily in Australia.

Businesswoman Anna Mowbray and her husband, former All Blacks player Ali Williams, pitched a new private league for 2027, but negotiations fell through just eight weeks after signing a term sheet.

"I don't understand my life without netball," said Mason. "It's been a big part of my identity, and [there is a] mental toll to [being] continually knocked down.

"I think of everything in this whole situation as just completely sad."

Nathan Limm, who has been following the story for the New Zealand Herald said: "The Ferns' success feels a little bit fragile. They get a few injuries, where's the depth underneath if they're not playing domestic netball?

"I'm not confident there will be a league next year. The communication between Netball NZ and the Players Association, with their investors, with the public, has been so rocky.

"I think there is a real distinct lack of trust between the players and Netball NZ."

When asked whether there are plans for a domestic netball competition next season New Zealand Netball said: "Work on an elite domestic competition for 2027 is well under way. Our goal is a sustainable, professional competition for 2027 and beyond."

Source: BBC Sport | Published: 2026-11-25 07:17 UTC

item.title: Villeneuve: Verstappen showed 'race craft' edge over Mercedes pair in Vegas
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source. (Clean-up failed for this item, so the body is a truncated excerpt of the original.)

Max Verstappen showed 'race craft' edge over George Russell and Kimi Antonelli during Las Vegas GP, says Jacques Villeneuve

Max Verstappen withstood pressure from Mercedes' George Russell and Kimi Antonelli on his way to winning a thrilling Las Vegas GP for Red Bull; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports this weekend, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday

Tuesday 24 November 2026 21:25, UK

Former Formula 1 world champion Jacques Villeneuve says Max Verstappen's Las Vegas Grand Prix victory showed that Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and George Russell will not be able to beat the Red Bull driver in next year's championship unless they have a superior car.

Verstappen retained the lead from pole position at the start but was challenged by Russell and then later Antonelli for almost the entire 50-lap race amid near constant changes of position throughout the field, but the Red Bull driver expertly saw off their best efforts before both made late errors to drop down the order.

Antonelli has already been crowned 2026 world champion after Mercedes' dominance early in the season helped him build a significant advantage, but Verstappen is putting together an ominous finish to the year, with the four-time world champion having won four of the last six races and claimed nine successive podiums.

- F1 2026 Calendar | F1 2026 Standings | F1 Gossip Column

- Got the Sky Sports app? Sign up for latest F1 alerts📱

- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream F1 with no contract 📺

Sky Sports F1 pundit and 1997 F1 world champion Villeneuve said after the race: "It was exciting. People will say there was a battery involved [in all the passes], but it doesn't matter.

"We saw some race craft. Max was above and the two Mercedes drivers were lacking in that respect.

"And what it is telling us is that unless next year Mercedes have a car that's superior, they can't win because there's something missing."

A combination of factors, most notably the extreme power of the slipstream effect, meant there were more than 350 overtakes during a breathless race at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit.

The lead changed hands 34 times, but every time Verstappen was overtaken, which on almost every occasion was by a Mercedes, the four-time world champion retook his position within a few corners.

Russell locked up and hit a barrier as he tried to pass Antonelli for second in the closing stages, before the Italian suffered a loss of power at the start of the final lap after incorrectly lifting off the throttle as he was preparing to mount a final challenge to Verstappen.

Villeneuve was also impressed by the drives of seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton and last year's title winner Lando Norris, who took advantage of the Mercedes errors to finish second ahead of his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri.

Hamilton could have also ended up on the podium had it not been for him spinning in a contentious collision with his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc.

"You could see that Lewis had good race craft as well as Lando," Villeneuve added.

"It was really fun to see. We saw today a race where you don't need pit stops, you don't need tyres that degrade.

"We had a race where drivers could push like qualifying laps all the time and that allowed them to race. It was great fun."

item.title: Wales need strong finish to campaign - Morgan
item.description:

Wales need strong finish to campaign - Morgan

Jac Morgan is keen to finish the job with Wales against Japan so that the 2026 Nations Championship can be declared a success.

Steve Tandy's men finished fifth in the northern hemisphere table, but that does not reflect the strides made in November.

Wales famously beat New Zealand and were edged out by Australia after starting the month with a nervy win against Japan.

The triumph against the All Blacks has secured a place in history, but failure to beat the Brave Blossoms at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on Saturday (13:10 GMT) would take some of the shine off the campaign.

"It is important that we finish off on a bit of a high," said Morgan, who started all three Cardiff fixtures at open-side flanker.

"We have been good in a lot of areas over the last couple of weeks, but there are always places where we can get better.

"It has been a positive few weeks, but we still have a job to do against Japan and want to put in a big performance we are proud of."

- Wales look to World Cup when taking on Japan

- A world-class winger - Louis Rees-Zammit 2.0

Wales must go from the raucous backing of the Principality Stadium crowd to being the first part of a Twickenham double-header.

They are the warm-up act before England host New Zealand a fortnight after Wales made history by ending the 73-year wait for a win against the All Blacks. England are themselves hoping to complete a back-to-back double against Dave Rennie's side.

"New Zealand was a special day to be a part of. It's given the boys a lot of confidence and it's something we want to build on," said Morgan.

Tandy is set to freshen up his side to face Japan with Morgan one of 11 players who started all three home Tests.

Fitness permitting, the Gloucester flanker is a certainty for the Six Nations opener against France in Paris on 6 February.

But Morgan is confident that Wales will show their greater squad depth and competition for places at Twickenham this weekend.

"Those who haven't played have been challenging and competitive to prepare the other boys," he said.

"Full credit to the whole squad, there is a great group here and we are always pushing to get better."

Wales play Japan for the fifth time in 16 months and will expect to win more convincingly than they did at the start of the month, when they nervously held on for a 28-21 victory.

Tandy's men have since performed well against New Zealand and Australia while Japan conceded 24 tries in heavy losses against England and Scotland.

Morgan said: "It wasn't the best of performances against Japan, but we have been building over the last few weeks and are looking forward to this weekend.

"We know how tough it will be because we have played Japan a few times over the last couple of years and every game has been close and tough."

Source: BBC Sport | Published: 2026-11-25 06:34 UTC

item.title: Are Man Utd this season's Tottenham?
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Are Manchester United this season's Tottenham?

Last season, Tottenham - a member of the so-called 'big six' - escaped relegation from the Premier League on the final day.

Now, with Manchester United making their worst start to a league season since 1972, it begs the question: are United this season's Spurs?

Well while Tottenham finished 17th with just 41 points, they actually started the season better than United have. After 11 games last season, Spurs were riding high in fifth with 18 points - 10 more than United have now.

But one of the biggest myths in football is 'the table never lies' and it was certainly lying about Tottenham at this stage last season.

While the table was prompting talk of a possible Champions League place, expected goals (xG) had already recognised a relegation battle lay ahead for Tottenham, even predicting the position they'd finish in.

United's expected goal difference is almost identical to Tottenham's at this stage last season, but this time the table is more honest, even if United are perhaps not as bad as it makes out.

But there's no denying United's statistics are those of a team in a relegation battle, with many of them in the bottom six of Premier League teams this season.

While United have performed poorly defensively, their attack is actually not bad.

Remarkably, United have taken the most shots in the Premier League so far this season, and their expected goals scored figure is in the top five.

But what new head coach Mauricio Pochettino has to implement quickly is some quality control when it comes to shots at both ends of the pitch. United are converting just 7% of their chances and conceding 16% of their opponents' - a poor combination for any team.

And it's not simply down to finishing or shot-stopping, though they should have scored a few more. Based on xG per shot, United are currently taking the second-worst chances to score and giving up the easiest ones at the back.

As a result, Opta give United just over a one-in-four chance of being relegated at the end of the season (27.5%), making them the fifth-most likely side to go down after Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Ipswich and Coventry.

By analysing historical and team performances as well as the strength of opponents, Opta predict the % chance of each club finishing in each position in the League.

While the above means it's more likely United will survive, it's worth noting the one position Opta predicts United are most likely to finish is 18th, with a 10.1% chance. That would mean the 13-time Premier League winners are relegated.

There's a 90% chance they finish anywhere else, but the next most likely are the three places just above the relegation zone, including a 9.9% chance of them finishing where Tottenham did last season.

History also suggests a relegation battle lies ahead for United given their poor start.

Of the 26 previous sides that had exactly eight points after 11 games, 13 survived and 13 were relegated. Among those that stayed up, only four finished more than six points above the danger zone.

A top-half finish looks unlikely. Since the competition became a 20-team league in 1995-96, no side has ever finished in the top half after taking eight points or fewer from their first 11 games.

Two teams did finish there more than 30 years ago but they had four more games to climb the table as teams played 42 games a season in those days.

Having said that, both were in the top half at the 38-game mark so United finishing there wouldn't be entirely unprecedented.

It's a big ask, though, as the club have already taken 19 points fewer from the fixtures they've played than they did last season.

Even if they were to repeat the results that led to them finishing third from now on, they would still only reach 52 points, the number Chelsea narrowly finished 10th with last season

Though United are without a win in nine Premier League matches, their remaining fixtures of 2026 do offer some hope.

While they have a tough home game against Brentford this weekend and a trip to champions Arsenal just before Christmas, their other five games are against teams currently in the bottom seven - sides we must, at this point, call relegation rivals

So despite suffering the worst first game by a Manchester United manager for 100 years in the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, Pochettino will hope to quickly quash any concerns his new club will be embroiled in the same fight as his former one last season.

Source: BBC Sport | Published: 2026-11-25 06:22 UTC

item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

WTGL: Charley Hull 'has great laugh' on Atlanta Drive debut despite defeat to Lottie Woad's Boston Common

Wednesday 25 November 2026 06:41, UK

Charley Hull tasted defeat on WTGL debut as her Atlanta Drive side lost 8-3 to Lottie Woad's Boston Common at the SoFi Center in Florida.

English star Hull won her first singles match in the competition, beating Solheim Cup team-mate Celine Boutier as she holed a 15-foot return putt having shot an initial effort way past the hole.

But Atlanta Drive were still soundly defeated in their first game of the inaugural women's season as Boston Common bounced back from last week's loss to Motor City.

- Women's TGL - results and schedule for debut season

Still Hull, who smoked her opening tee shot 264 yards, thoroughly enjoyed the experience, saying: "Obviously it wasn't the result that we wanted, but we had a great laugh. I know we're not on the golf course, but you're in the golf environment."

Hull's first experience of the WTGL came after a whirlwind few days in which she finished tied 23rd at the LPGA's season-ending Tour Championship and then took part in a shoot with equipment manufacturer TaylorMade.

The 30-year-old said she was "massively flagging" but will now enjoy some downtime with her family at Disney World.

Woad, whose spectacular chip-in against Motor City had taken that clash into overtime, recorded a singles victory over Atlanta's Nataliya Guseva on Tuesday evening.

With Ina Yoon also thumping Andrea Lee, Boston picked up four points to Atlanta's one in the singles having opened up a 4-2 lead after the triples leg.

Yoon secured the win for Boston when she landed her tee shot at the par-three 14th to inside three feet, earning three points with two Hammers in play.

Earlier on, Boutier chipped in from just off the green to put Boston 4-0 up after eight holes of triples before Atlanta chalked up their first two points at the ninth.

The WTGL continues with a double header on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, as Woad's Boston play New York from 6pm UK before Hull's Atlanta Drive meet unbeaten Motor City from 8.30pm UK.

Source: Sky Sports | Published: 2026-11-25 06:13 UTC

item.title: Hysa aims to win WBC title then take on 'favourite fighter' Fury
item.description:

Nelson Hysa aims to beat Agit Kabayel, win WBC world title and take on Tyson Fury, his 'favourite fighter'

Nelson Hysa challenges Agit Kabayel for the WBC title on Saturday in Dusseldorf; Hard-punching Hysa hopes to upset popular German Kabayel and then look to take on his 'favourite fighter' Tyson Fury; Hysa says Moses Itauma is still the best in the division - 'I don't want to fight him!'

Tuesday 24 November 2026 19:23, UK

Nelson Hysa has a vision. He wants to dethrone Agit Kabayel, win the WBC heavyweight world title and then take on his favourite fighter – Tyson Fury.

Hysa, unbeaten in 25 professional fights, challenges Kabayel on Saturday for the WBC heavyweight world championship.

The Albanian has taken 23 of those wins inside the distance and is looking to upset the popular German when they fight in Dusseldorf this weekend.

A power-puncher, Hysa told Sky Sports: "The knockout was with me from the first day that I started boxing.

"In this match [against Kabayel] I am preparing to do more good rounds because I know the opponent is a very good boxer, he's a tough boxer, a serious boxer.

"But we are planning, we are trying to do our best. We have our strategy to win the match and I think we will win the match earlier than the 12th round.

"I need to move up the ratio of knockouts!"

With Oleksandr Usyk vacating his championships, there are now new belt-holders in the division, but Hysa does not consider Kabayel the best of the current heavyweight titlists.

"For me No 1 now of the guys that have the belts, No 1 is Filip Hrgovic, [then Daniel] Dubois and for me the special one is Tyson Fury.

"Hrgovic will do very good because he's a good boxer," Hysa added. "Hrgovic beat the best guy in the heavyweight division. He beat Moses [Itauma]. I don't want to do a fight with Moses, he's a good guy! He will be the best heavyweight in the world. He is the best heavyweight in the world but he needs more time."

Fury will fight Anthony Joshua for the WBA 'super' heavyweight title when they meet on December 11. Hysa tips Fury to win and is eager to box him in a unification if he comes through his own fight.

"Who doesn't want to fight Tyson Fury? He's a legend," Hysa said. "The No 1 man at heavyweight.

"He's my No 1 favourite boxer, I love him, I love everything he does. His style, everything.

"Who doesn't want to fight Tyson Fury?"

Source: Sky Sports | Published: 2026-11-25 06:00 UTC
